meta.description: Australian energy rebate & incentive dataset for the TradieAutomate Rebate Finder. Maintained by the Bonsai maintenance cron — diff against source pages listed per program, update amounts/eligibility/status, bump last_verified. NEVER invent figures; when a source page contradicts this file, the source wins.

vic_solar_homes_hot_water.name: Solar Homes Hot Water Rebate
vic_solar_homes_hot_water.amount_note: 50% of purchase price after STCs and VEECs, capped at $1,000; $1,400 cap for eligible locally-made systems (from 1 July 2025).
eligibility: Victorian owner-occupier of an existing property
Household taxable income under $150,000 (from 1 July 2026)
Property value under $3 million
Replacing a hot water system at least 3 years old
No prior hot water or battery rebate at the address
Not for new builds or rentals
vic_solar_homes_hot_water.how_to_claim: Apply via an authorised hot water retailer; rebate applied after STCs and VEECs.

vic_veu_hot_water.name: Victorian Energy Upgrades — Hot Water Discount
vic_veu_hot_water.amount_range: Up to $560 (heat pump) / up to $700 (efficient upgrade)
vic_veu_hot_water.amount_note: VEU discount on approved heat pump or solar hot water systems via an accredited provider. Works alongside the Solar Homes rebate.
eligibility: Victorian household or business
Install in a home or building at least 2 years old
VEU-approved product installed by accredited provider
vic_veu_hot_water.how_to_claim: Order an approved appliance through a VEU-accredited installer — discount applied at point of sale.

vic_solar_pv.name: Solar Homes Solar Panel Rebate
vic_solar_pv.amount_note: Plus optional interest-free loan. Rebate amounts held steady from 1 July 2026; households earning $150K-$210K no longer eligible from 1 July 2026.
eligibility: Victorian owner-occupier
Household income under threshold (per Solar Victoria current rules)
Existing property, not new build
vic_solar_pv.how_to_claim: Apply through Solar Victoria; panels must be on the approved product list and installed by approved retailer.

vic_battery_loan.name: Solar Homes Battery Loan (closed to new applications)
vic_battery_loan.amount_range: Interest-free loan — no longer accepting applications
vic_battery_loan.amount_note: Solar Victoria no longer takes applications for interest-free solar battery loans. Battery buyers fall back to federal programs.
vic_battery_loan.how_to_claim: N/A — see federal Cheaper Home Batteries Program instead.

nsw_ess_hot_water.name: Energy Savings Scheme — Hot Water Upgrade Incentive
nsw_ess_hot_water.amount_range: Up to $640 (electric to heat pump) / up to $330 (gas to heat pump)
nsw_ess_hot_water.amount_note: Upfront discount applied in the quote by participating installers. Actual discount varies by system size ($200-$800 typical).
eligibility: NSW households and small businesses
Replacing an existing electric resistance or gas hot water system
Installed by ESS-accredited provider
System meets minimum efficiency requirements
nsw_ess_hot_water.how_to_claim: Get a quote from an ESS-registered provider showing the discount applied.

nsw_home_energy_saver.name: Home Energy Saver
nsw_home_energy_saver.amount_range: Up to $4,000 discount or $15,000 zero-interest loan
nsw_home_energy_saver.amount_note: Successor to Empowering Homes (closed 2024). Covers home batteries, insulation and other efficiency upgrades.
eligibility: NSW households
Technology must be on the eligible list (e.g. home batteries)
nsw_home_energy_saver.how_to_claim: Apply through participating providers / Service NSW referral.

nsw_vpp.name: Virtual Power Plant (VPP) Battery Incentive
nsw_vpp.amount_note: Sign your battery up to a demand-response contract; paid for making stored energy available at peak times.
eligibility: NSW households with an eligible battery
Join a participating VPP
nsw_vpp.how_to_claim: Register with a participating VPP operator.

qld_battery_booster.name: Battery Booster (closed)
qld_battery_booster.amount_note: Offered up to $4,000 to households under income caps. No replacement announced as of August 2026.
qld_battery_booster.how_to_claim: N/A — use federal Cheaper Home Batteries Program instead.

fed_cheaper_home_batteries.name: Cheaper Home Batteries Program (federal)
fed_cheaper_home_batteries.amount_note: Administered by the Clean Energy Regulator. Point-of-sale reduction on eligible 5-100 kWh battery systems; battery must be VPP-capable and on the approved list.
eligibility: Battery 5 kWh to 100 kWh nominal capacity (STCs on first 50 kWh)
Must be paired with rooftop solar (new or existing)
Approved product list, VPP-capable
Installed by accredited installer
One claim per property
No income test
fed_cheaper_home_batteries.how_to_claim: Ask your installer to apply the discount at point of sale — no application form.

fed_stc_solar.name: Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) — Solar Panel Discount
fed_stc_solar.amount_note: Federal discount on solar PV and hot water; STCs assigned to the installer in exchange for an upfront price reduction. QLD earns slightly more due to sunnier zone.
eligibility: Australian households/businesses
Eligible system on Clean Energy Regulator register
Installed by accredited installer
fed_stc_solar.expiry: Scales down annually (rate step-down continues to 2030)
fed_stc_solar.how_to_claim: Ask for STC discount as a separate line on the quote.

fed_stc_hot_water.name: Federal STC Discount — Heat Pump & Solar Hot Water
fed_stc_hot_water.amount_note: The federal STC discount is the main hot water incentive in QLD, WA, SA, TAS and NT — none of these states has its own state heat pump rebate in 2026 (QLD's Climate Smart Energy Savers closed December 2023, TAS's Energy Saver Loan Scheme closed September 2025). Taken off the installer's quote.
eligibility: Australian residents
Registered heat pump/solar hot water model
STCs created within 12 months of install
fed_stc_hot_water.how_to_claim: Ask the installer to show the STC discount as a separate line on the quote.

sa_reps_vpp.name: REPS Virtual Power Plant Incentive
sa_reps_vpp.amount_note: South Australia's Home Battery Scheme closed in September 2022. The Retailer Energy Productivity Scheme (REPS) still offers a VPP incentive worth up to about $2,050 (2026 reporting) — delivered through participating energy retailers as part of a VPP deal, not a government application. Stacks with the federal program.
eligibility: South Australian household or business
Eligible battery connected to an approved demand-response aggregator or VPP
Join through a participating energy retailer
sa_reps_vpp.expiry: Ongoing — value and terms set by retailer
sa_reps_vpp.how_to_claim: Contact participating SA energy retailers for a VPP battery deal.

wa_residential_battery.name: WA Residential Battery Scheme
wa_residential_battery.amount_note: One of Australia's strongest battery schemes: rebates up to $1,300 for Synergy customers and up to $3,800 for Horizon Power customers (based on 10 kWh usable capacity; larger batteries still get the max), plus no-interest loans up to $10,000 for households earning under $210,000 (up to 10-year terms). Stacks with the federal Cheaper Home Batteries Program. VPP participation required.
eligibility: WA household (Synergy or Horizon Power network)
New, VPP-capable battery on the Supported Solutions List
Installed by an accredited installer (Plenti Vendor Directory)
Commit to a VPP product from your retailer
Loan requires combined household income under $210,000
wa_residential_battery.expiry: Until all 100,000 rebates distributed — expected to 2027
wa_residential_battery.how_to_claim: Get quotes from approved battery retailers; rebate applied as upfront discount.

act_sustainable_household.name: Sustainable Household Scheme
act_sustainable_household.amount_note: The ACT has no battery or hot water rebate — it offers cheap money instead. Low-interest loans for batteries, heat pumps, efficient appliances and EV chargers: $2,000-$20,000 (ceiling rising from $15,000 to $20,000 from 1 July 2026), repaid over up to 10 years, at 3% for general applicants since 1 July 2025. Finance, not a rebate — stacks with federal programs.
eligibility: ACT homeowner
Eligible upgrade (battery, heat pump, solar, EV charger, appliances)
Attend scheme energy-efficiency requirements
act_sustainable_household.how_to_claim: Apply through the ACT Government — loans repaid via your electricity bill.

act_hot_water_rebate.name: ACT Hot Water Rebate (concession holders)
act_hot_water_rebate.amount_note: ACT homeowners with an eligible concession card can get 50% of the cost (up to $2,500) of a heat pump or evacuated-tube solar hot water system, within a total of up to $5,000 in rebates. Everyone else uses the Sustainable Household Scheme loan.
eligibility: ACT homeowner with eligible concession card
Heat pump or evacuated-tube solar hot water system
act_hot_water_rebate.how_to_claim: Apply via the ACT Home Energy Support program.

tas_energy_saver.name: Energy Saver Loan Scheme (closed)
tas_energy_saver.amount_note: Tasmania's Energy Saver Loan Scheme (interest-free finance up to $10,000 for energy-efficient products) closed to new applications on 1 September 2025, earlier than planned. Tasmanian households now rely on the federal STC discount and Cheaper Home Batteries Program.

nt_battery_scheme.name: Home and Business Battery Scheme (closed)
nt_battery_scheme.amount_note: The NT Home and Business Battery Scheme reached its $6 million funding cap and is no longer taking applications. NT residents fall back to federal STCs and the (more limited) federal battery program rollout.
nt_battery_scheme.how_to_claim: N/A — check with local installers for current NT eligibility under federal programs.
